scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the inter-AS physical link on router2 (eth0) is down, which prevents the eBGP peering and inter-domain forwarding. Mechanism: with router2’s eth0 down, no L2/L3 connectivity exists on 193.10.11.0/24. Router2 cannot source or receive BGP keepalives to 193.10.11.1, so its BGP session transitions to Active and withdraws learned routes; traffic between LANs then blackholes at router1 due to failed next-hop resolution. Localization: router2 eth0 shows administratively down and no carrier (ip addr shows eth0 state DOWN with no UP/RUNNING flags; ifconfig flags 4098 <BROADCAST,MULTICAST>; ethtool reports “Link detected: no”). Router2 cannot even ping 193.10.11.1 (“Network is unreachable”), and router1 cannot reach 193.10.11.2 (“Destination Host Unreachable”). Router2’s “show bgp summary” confirms the session is down (Active). Router1 still shows a BGP-learned 200.1.1.0/24 and neighbor up ~2 minutes; that’s consistent with the failure occurring very recently and router1’s hold timer not expiring yet or stale state prior to withdrawal. Root cause: router2’s inter-AS interface eth0 was left administratively down or lost its physical link. Corrective fix: restore router2 eth0—ensure the cable/virtual link is present and bring the interface up (ip link set eth0 up). Verify carrier (ethtool shows Link detected: yes), confirm bidirectional ping on 193.10.11.x, and ensure eBGP re-establishes and routes between 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 are exchanged. Consider enabling BFD for faster failure detection.
